headlines.article_text: Moderna has been on a tear since mid-August. Citi now sees it plunging 60% Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu It's time for Moderna shareholders to bail on the stock, according to Citi. Analyst Geoff Meacham downgraded the biotech name to sell. He raised his price target to $80 from $60, though that implies 60% downside from Tuesday's close. Moderna has been on a tear since Aug. 19 , when the company announced positive late-stage trial results for an experimental personalized cancer vaccine known as intismeran autogene. The drug, combined with Merck's Keytruda, met goals in more than 1,100 patients with higher-risk or advanced melanoma. Moderna shares have rallied 223% since the trial results were released. MRNA mountain 2026-08-19 MRNA since Aug. 19 However, Meacham thinks the stock is now trading at unsustainable levels. "We struggle to justify the valuation through public-company comparisons or pipeline [net present value]," he wrote to clients. "Moderna's ~$80B market cap approximates Regeneron's despite materially lower expected revenue and earnings. On NPV, assigning 100% [probability of success] to intismeran's lead oncology programs supports only ~$100/sh, or 50% below current levels. Reaching ~$200/sh requires ~$26B in annual oncology sales ($13B to Moderna), nearly 7x our model." "Melanoma is highly responsive to checkpoint inhibition, making it a favorable setting for providing proof-of-concept. Renal, lung, and bladder cancer could create value, but each presents distinct tumor biology," Meacham added. "Overall, we believe that based on aggressive implied sales and unrealistic PoS assumptions, the current valuation is unjustifiable with a negatively skewed risk/reward profile." Moderna shares closed at $203.46 on Tuesday. They fell nearly 6% in premarket trading Wednesday. The company did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. Most analysts are on the sidelines when it comes to Moderna. LSEG data shows that 15 of 24 rate the stock as a buy, while six assigned buy or strong buy ratings. The remaining three have underperform ratings.

Christopher Pike | Bloomberg | Getty Images Aircraft manufacturer Boeing rose in premarket trading Wednesday after securing a deal with the U.S. Pentagon and U.S. Navy to develop the next generation of fighter jets. The contract, worth more than $20 billion, is to build its Sixth-Generation F/A-XX Strike Fighter over a long-term phase, the defense departments said . The F/A-XX is intended to replace the service's fleet of F/A-18 Super Hornets. The fighter will advance open mission systems architecture, advanced mission systems, and operational reach and capacity, Boeing said in a separate statement. Boeing was last up 3.1% in premarket trading. Shares of Northrop Grumman Corporation , a top U.S. aerospace and defense contractor and a Boeing competitor, were down 3.5% in premarket. F/A-XX will dominate contested airspace, extend operational reach, and deliver a decisive combat advantage for the warfighter," said Michael P. Duffey, Under Secretary of War for acquisition and sustainment. It marks the company's second prestigious sixth-generation jet contract in a year after the Air Force selected it to develop its F-47 fighter in 2025.
